q: 1. The mass per unit volume of a liquid at a standard temperature and pressure is called
explain: Mass density (ρ) is defined as the mass of a substance per unit volume. In contrast, specific weight is weight per unit volume.

q: 2. The weight per unit volume of a liquid at a standard temperature and pressure is called
explain: Specific weight (w or γ) represents the force exerted by gravity on a unit volume of a fluid.

q: 3. The specific weight of water in S.I. units is taken as
explain: All these values are equivalent: 9.81 kN/m³ = 9810 N/m³. Converting to mm³, it becomes 9.81 x 10⁻⁶ N/mm³.

q: 4. The ratio of specific weight of a liquid to the specific weight of pure water at a standard temperature is called
explain: Specific gravity (S) is a dimensionless ratio comparing a liquid's density or specific weight to that of a standard fluid (water at 4°C).

q: 5. The specific gravity of water is taken as
explain: Water is the standard reference for liquids, so its specific gravity is defined as 1.

q: 6. The specific weight of sea water is _________ that of pure water
explain: Sea water contains dissolved salts, making it denser and heavier per unit volume than pure water.

q: 7. The mass of 2.5 m³ of a certain liquid is 2 tonnes. Its mass density is
explain: Density = Mass / Volume. 2 tonnes = 2000 kg. So, 2000 / 2.5 = 800 kg/m³.

q: 8. The specific gravity of an oil whose specific weight is 7.85 kN/m³, is
explain: Specific Gravity = Specific weight of oil / Specific weight of water = 7.85 / 9.81 ≈ 0.8.

q: 9. A vessel of 4 m³ contains an oil which weights 30 kN. The specific weight of the oil is
explain: Specific weight = Total Weight / Total Volume = 30 kN / 4 m³ = 7.5 kN/m³.

q: 10. The property of a liquid which offers resistance to the movement of one layer of liquid over another adjacent layer of liquid, is called
explain: Viscosity is the internal friction of a fluid that resists the relative motion of its layers.

q: 11. The force per unit length is the unit of
explain: Surface tension is defined as the force acting per unit length (N/m) along the surface of a liquid.

q: 12. The variation in the volume of a liquid with the variation of pressure is called
explain: Compressibility is the measure of the relative volume change of a fluid as a response to a pressure change.

q: 13. A glass tube of smaller diameter is used while performing an experiment for the capillary rise of water because
options: it is easier to see through the glass tube
glass tube is cheaper than a metallic tube
it is not possible to conduct this experiment with any other tube
explain: While small diameters increase the height of capillary rise (making it measurable), glass is used specifically for its transparency to allow for clear observation of the meniscus.

q: 14. The mercury does not wet the glass. This is due to the property of the liquid known as
explain: Mercury has higher cohesive forces (attraction between its own molecules) than adhesive forces (attraction to glass), causing it to avoid 'wetting' the surface.

q: 15. With an increase in size of tube, the rise or depression of liquid in the tube due to surface tension will
options: depend upon the characteristics of liquid
explain: Capillary rise (h) is inversely proportional to the diameter of the tube (d) according to the formula h = (4σ cosθ) / (ρgd).

q: 16. The unit of surface tension is
explain: As it represents the force acting along a line on the surface, its SI unit is Newtons per metre (N/m).

q: 17. Falling drops of water become spheres due to the property of
explain: Surface tension acts to minimize the surface area of a liquid volume; a sphere has the minimum surface area for a given volume.

q: 18. The intensity of pressure at point, in a liquid, is
options: directly proportional to the area of the vessel containing liquid
directly proportional to the depth of liquid from the surface
directly proportional to the length of the vessel containing liquid
inversely proportional to the depth of liquid from the surface
explain: According to hydrostatic law, P = ρgh, meaning pressure increases linearly with depth (h).

q: 19. The pressure intensity in kN/m² (or kPa) at any point in a liquid is
explain: Pressure (P) is the product of specific weight (w) and depth (h).

q: 20. The pressure at a point 4 m below the free surface of water is
explain: P = wh = 9.81 kN/m³ * 4 m = 39.24 kN/m² (kPa).

q: 21. The height of a water column equivalent to a pressure of 0.15 MPa is
explain: h = P / w. Converting 0.15 MPa to 150 kPa: 150 / 9.81 ≈ 15.3 m.

q: 22. When the pressure intensity at point is more than the local atmospheric pressure, then the difference of these two pressure is called
explain: Gauge pressure is measured relative to atmospheric pressure. If it is higher, it is specifically called positive gauge pressure.

q: 23. The absolute pressure is equal to
explain: Absolute pressure is the total pressure measured from a perfect vacuum (zero reference).

q: 24. The pressure less than atmospheric pressure is known as
explain: All these terms describe pressures below the local atmospheric level.

q: 25. The pressure of a liquid measured with the help of a piezometer tube is
explain: A piezometer measures the pressure head relative to the atmosphere, thus providing gauge pressure.

q: 26. The pressure measured with the help of a piezometer tube is in
explain: A piezometer measures pressure by the vertical height (h) to which the liquid rises in the tube.

q: 27. A piezometer tube is used only for measuring
explain: Piezometers are unsuitable for very high pressures (tube would be too long) or vacuum pressures (air would enter the tube).

q: 28. The liquid used in manometers should have
explain: High-density liquids (like mercury) allow for shorter manometer tubes when measuring high pressures.

q: 29. A manometer is used to measure
options: difference of pressures between two points in a pipe
explain: While differential manometers measure pressure differences, a standard manometer (like a U-tube) is used for point pressure in pipes/channels.

q: 30. A manometer is used to measure
explain: Manometers are generally employed for measuring higher pressures compared to simple piezometers.

q: 31. A differential manometer is used to measure
options: difference of pressures between two points in a pipe
explain: The specific purpose of a differential manometer is to determine the pressure head difference between two distinct points.

q: 32. The total pressure on a horizontally immersed surface is
explain: Total pressure (P) = specific weight (w) * Area (A) * depth of centroid (x̄).

q: 33. The total pressure on an immersed surface inclined at an angle θ with the liquid surface is
explain: Total pressure is independent of the angle of inclination and depends only on the area and the depth of the centroid.

q: 34. The point at which the resultant pressure on an immersed surface acts, is known as
explain: The Centre of Pressure is the point where the total hydrostatic force is considered to act.

q: 35. The depth of centre of pressure (h̄) for a vertically immersed surface from the liquid surface is given by
explain: This is the standard formula derived using the parallel axis theorem for pressure distribution.

q: 36. The centre of pressure for a vertically immersed surface lies at a distance equal to _________ the centre of gravity.
explain: The centre of pressure always lies below the centre of gravity because pressure increases with depth.

q: 37. The depth of centre of pressure for an immersed surface inclined at an angle θ with the liquid surface lies at a distance equal to _________ the centre of gravity.
explain: For inclined surfaces, the vertical distance below the centroid is adjusted by the sin² θ component.

q: 38. A vertical wall is subjected to a pressure due to one kind of liquid, on one of its sides. The total pressure on the wall per unit length is
explain: P = w * Area * x̄. For unit length (1m) and depth H, Area = H * 1 and x̄ = H/2. Thus, P = wH²/2.

40. A vertical wall is subjected to a pressure due to one kind of liquid, on one of its sides. The total pressure on the wall acts at a distance _________ from the liquid surface.
explain: The centre of pressure for a rectangular vertical surface is at 2/3 of the depth from the top (free surface).

q: 41. When a vertical wall is subjected to pressures due to liquid on both sides, the resultant pressure is the _________ of the two pressures.
explain: Forces act in opposite directions, so the net force is the difference between the pressures on each side.

q: 42. In a lockgate, the reaction between two gates is
explain: The reaction R at the hinge/meeting point is calculated as P / (2 sin α) based on force equilibrium.

q: 43. The water pressure per metre length on a vertical masonary wall of dam is
explain: This follows the same logic as Q.38 for the total hydrostatic force on a vertical surface.

q: 44. When a body is placed over a liquid, it will sink down if
options: gravitational force is equal to the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is less than the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is more than the upthrust of the liquid
explain: If the downward weight exceeds the upward buoyant force, the body will have a net downward acceleration.

q: 45. When a body is placed over a liquid, it will float if
options: gravitational force is equal to the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is less than the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is more than the upthrust of the liquid
explain: A body floats when its weight is less than or equal to the maximum possible upthrust (weight of the fully displaced volume).

q: 46. When a body is immersed wholly or partially in a liquid, it is lifted up by a force equal to weight of liquid displaced by the body. This statement is called
explain: This is the fundamental definition of Archimedes' Principle regarding buoyancy.

q: 47. The centre of gravity of the volume of the liquid displaced is called
explain: The buoyant force acts through the centroid of the displaced volume, known as the Centre of Buoyancy.

q: 48. The buoyancy depends upon the
options: pressure with which the liquid is displaced
explain: According to Archimedes' Principle, the magnitude of the buoyant force is exactly equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.

q: 49. A uniform body 3 m long, 2 m wide and 1 m deep floats in water. If the depth of immersion is 0.6 m, then the weight of the body is
explain: Weight = Displaced volume * w = (3 * 2 * 0.6) * 9.81 = 3.6 * 9.81 ≈ 35.3 kN.

q: 50. When a body, floating in a liquid, is given a small angular displacement, it starts oscillating about a point known as
explain: The Metacentre is the point of intersection of the vertical through the new centre of buoyancy and the original axis of the body.
